From: TaxAdvisor BV <tax@eutaxconsulting.com>

Subject: RE: Solaria VAT validation & reverse-charge applicability

Hi Laura / Marissa,

Quick clarifications from a tax perspective (we advise Solaria):
- Reverse-charge applies for B2B cross-border services within the EU when the customer is VAT-registered in another member state and the supplier is established in a different EU member state. The invoice must show both VAT numbers and include the phrase 'reverse charge — VAT to be accounted for by the recipient' (or equivalent local language).
- Self-billing is permitted, but the supplier (Redwood) must have a signed agreement and keep the same invoice records; the buyer must be able to demonstrate accounting entries for VAT.
- Important operational note: If Redwood's billing entity for this customer is a Redwood GmbH registered in DE, reverse-charge still applies only if the customer is in another member state. If Redwood bills from Redwood US, different rules apply (OSS, place of supply). Please confirm which legal entity will issue invoices for Solaria.

We can confirm Solaria's VAT ID (DE123456789) is valid; the attached certificate is the official one. We are happy to sign a power-of-attorney letter if needed for VIES checks and will coordinate any local evidence.

Regards,
TaxAdvisor BV (Eva L. Müller)
European VAT Consulting
